positions.as_written: Measure alignment on a standing long leg film rather than on a knee radiograph, since the landmarks are off the smaller film.
Treat the mechanical axis as a predictor of load share rather than as a measurement of load.
Plan from a standardised standing long leg film, and state the rotation control used.
Avoid inferring dynamic load from a static angle in an individual, since the correlation is moderate.
State the convention used when quoting a hip knee ankle angle, since sign conventions differ between publications.

Take the patient's age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations into any correction decision, because the angle describes a limb and not a person.
